Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Rust web application. Start in the `/app` Git repository: it has a minimal Cargo project (`quizzy`) and no app yet. Rust (stable), Cargo, SQLite (the library and the CLI), and Chromium are installed. You can download crates from crates.io; other network access is blocked. Fetch and build all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the build, the database, and so on) and runs the app in release mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`. It must work offline (for example, `cargo build --release --offline`), and it should start in a few minutes at most.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

The game works, and now we want prizes.

The quiz settings get a new field, "Number of winners" (a number, at least 1, 3 by default).

Scoring:

- Each correct answer gives one point.
- Players with equal points are ranked by speed: the total time of their correct answers wins when it is lower. The time of an answer runs from the moment the question opens to the player's last pick.
- Players don't see points during the game.

Speed now decides ties, so all players must get each question at the same moment: the big screen and the phones must follow the moderator close to instantly.

After "End quiz":

- The big screen shows the leaderboard: one list item for each player, in order, with the place, the name, and the points ("2 points", "1 point", "0 points").
- Each player's phone shows the place ("Place 2 of 5") and the points ("3 points").

Picking the winners (N is the number of winners):

- The "Top N" button (for example, "Top 3") makes the first N players of the leaderboard the winners.
- The "Draw" button is for ties. Every player with more points than the N-th place wins. The remaining prizes are drawn at random among the players with exactly the N-th place's points (speed doesn't matter here). Each click draws again.
- Players with 0 points never win. If fewer than N players have points, all of them win.
- The "Reset winners" button removes the winners.
- Winners get the "Winner" mark on the leaderboard, and their phones show "You won!". Both update live.

# Quizzy

A Rust/SQLite app for preparing conference quizzes, using the supplied Quizzy
mockups and local Inter font. Moderator pages live at `/moderate` and use HTTP
Basic authentication. No external services or CDN assets are used.

## Run

```sh
export PORT=3000
export SECRET_KEY_BASE='replace-with-a-long-random-secret'
export QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME='moderator'
export QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD='replace-with-your-password'
bin/serve
```

The launcher builds the locked dependencies **offline in release mode**, creates
`storage/` and initializes SQLite, then runs in the foreground on `0.0.0.0:$PORT`.
`GET /up` returns 200 once startup is complete. Data is stored in
`storage/quizzy.sqlite3`; stop the app before copying the whole storage directory
for a backup, or use SQLite's backup command while it is running.

Quizzes support question ordering, immediately saved Active checkboxes, multiple
correct options, and native delete confirmations. Preview is single-choice and
uses only active questions; answers and scores exist only in page memory.

## Play live

Open a quiz and choose **Start a game**. Share the full join URL or its QR code
with the room. Players enter **Your name** and **Join**, without accounts.

Use **Start**, **Finish**, **Next**, and finally **End quiz** on the moderator's
big screen. Phones and counters update live without reloads. Players can change
their choice while a question is open; correctness appears only after Finish.
Returning to the same link remembers the player. Each new game is independent
and snapshots only the quiz's active questions.

SQLite persists games, players, and final choices across restarts. Live presence
uses connection tracking and short heartbeat leases for unreliable Wi-Fi; saved
answers remain even if a player disconnects. The stage's answer counter is saved
answers / currently connected players. All assets, QR generation, and live
communications are local to this app.

## Reuse or share a quiz

Open a quiz and choose **Export**. Copy the JSON from the export page, then open
**Import quiz** on `/moderate`, paste it into **Quiz JSON**, and choose **Import**.
Every import creates a separate quiz, even when its title already exists. Exports
include only the title and ordered question/option contents (including inactive
questions), not database IDs or runtime data.

`active` defaults to `true` and `correct` to `false` when omitted on import; both
are always included in exports. Imports use the same validation as question forms:
nonblank question text, two or more nonblank options, and at least one correct
option. Blank option rows are skipped. Invalid input is retained with an error,
and the entire import is rejected without saving a quiz or any questions.


import time

    assert 'Number of winners' in request('/moderate/quizzes/new')[2], 'Missing prize setting'
    payload = {'title': 'Prizes regression', 'questions': [

    ]}

    assert status == 303
    quiz = headers['Location']
    try:
        assert post(quiz, {'title': payload['title'], 'number_of_winners': '2'}, token)[0] == 303
        game = post(quiz + '/games', {}, token)[1]['Location']
        link = '/play/' + game.rsplit('/', 1)[1]
        people = {name: Player() for name in ['Leader', 'Fast', 'Slow', 'Zero', 'Absent']}
        for name, p in people.items():
            assert p.request(link + '/join', {'name': name})[0] == 200
        def state(): return json.loads(request(game + '/state')[2])
        def control(action):
            status, _, body = post(game + '/action', {'action': action, 'version': state()['version']}, token)
            assert status == 200, body
            return json.loads(body)
        def pick(name, option):
            p = people[name]
            s = p.state(link)
            assert 'points' not in s and 'leaderboard' not in s
            assert p.request(link + '/answer', {'csrf': s['csrf'], 'question': s['index'], 'option': option})[0] == 200
        control('start')
        assert post(game + '/action', {'action': 'top', 'version': state()['version']}, token)[0] == 409
        # Slow's first pick must NOT be used: their last pick comes after Fast.

        time.sleep(.05)
        pick('Fast', 0)
        time.sleep(.05)
        pick('Slow', 1)
        pick('Slow', 0)
        pick('Leader', 0)
        pick('Zero', 1)
        control('finish')

            pick('Leader', 0)
